symptom: a crooked dinner-fork wrist and limited rotation in a young person
hook: the forearm bones had grown unevenly and bowed the wrist into a fork shape
whatYouSee: A short bowed radius with the ulna sticking out dorsally and the wrist bones wedged into a triangle that gives the dinner-fork shape.
whyItMatters: This growth plate disorder is often linked to Leri-Weill dyschondrosteosis and it causes wrist deformity and pain and reduced forearm rotation.
treatment: Management ranges from observation and physiotherapy to surgical correction with osteotomy or release of the abnormal tethering ligament.
takeaway: A dinner-fork wrist from an uneven bowed forearm in a young person is Madelung deformity.
